I refactored graph construction out of the graph type itself and into a dedicated builder. [graph/GraphBuilder.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/004_breadth_first_search/graph/GraphBuilder.java:7) now owns the mutable assembly phase with fluent `addDirectedEdge(...)`, `addUndirectedEdge(...)`, and `build()` methods, while [graph/AdjacencyListGraph.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/004_breadth_first_search/graph/AdjacencyListGraph.java:5) is now just an immutable `Graph` implementation. That removes the old `MutableGraph` abstraction entirely and gives the code a cleaner separation between building and consuming graphs.

I updated [graph/samples/SampleGraphs.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/004_breadth_first_search/graph/samples/SampleGraphs.java:7) to use the builder, so sample construction is now declarative and no longer tied to a mutable concrete graph object.
